Then, you can use the quadratic formula, x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a), to find the values of x. Plug in the values of a, b, and c into the formula, and simplify to find the solutions. Remember to check your work by plugging the solutions back into the original equation.

To find the stationary points of an equation y = f(x), you need to find the points where the derivative of the function is equal to zero. First, find the derivative of the function, f'(x). To find the y-coordinates, plug the x-values back into the original function, y = f(x).
